explanation: Copying/induction unit: fires on a token inside a phrase that is being repeated verbatim from earlier in the context (e.g. a title or name restated in the body, a #define repeating an #ifndef guard), especially mid-name subword pieces whose continuation is predictable from the earlier occurrence. Fires little on first occurrences or ordinary text.

Fires most strongly inside synthetic algebra word problems ("Let v be...", "Suppose...", "Solve..."), on 'Solve', minus signs, spaces and digits of equation terms; it also fires moderately on assorted boilerplate tokens (';' in GPL licence text, '.com' in addresses, HTML tags). Ordinary prose gives weak activation.

No single theme: strongest on 'remainder' in a math question, then on assorted code tokens (config keys, '.php', package path pieces, casts, 'function'), and on '-sex' in 'same-sex'. Hard to predict beyond 'code-ish syntax tokens' plus a few unrelated words.
Diffuse mixture: name endings (Turán), math/probability text tokens, code punctuation, place-name completions ('United States'), technical noun completions. No shared feature is evident.

Fires on the token that closes a header comment block, mainly ' */' or '*/' plus newline (or a closing '//' line) right after licence/copyright/author text at the top of a source file, just before code like #ifndef/package/namespace begins. Also an outlier on 'Kindle Edition'. Weak on prose.

Concealment/secrecy concept: fires on words meaning hidden or out of sight, such as 'hidden'/'Hidden', 'lurking', 'hiding', 'secret', 'implicit', 'buried', 'subtly', 'behind', 'deep down'. 'hidden' and 'lurking' fire strongest; related words like 'shadow', 'invisible' and 'behind the scenes' fire moderately.

Fires on the unit-of-measure token right after a number in scientific/biomedical measurements, especially the mass/amount part of concentration or dose units (mg, μg, g, mol in nmol/mmol, ng, mL, W/kg, cd). Time, length and money units after numbers fire weakly to moderately; the numbers themselves barely fire.

Mainly fires on the hyphen in a year range in copyright notices ('Copyright (C) 1997-1998', '2007-2017'), and somewhat on other range/separator dashes. A scattering of unrelated tokens in code and prose ('kidding', 'not', 'extends', error-code digits) also fires.

Fires on pieces of technical jargon in scientific or code contexts, such as the 'W' in compiler warning flags (-W...), 'parallel' after '#pragma omp', 'local' in 'Noetherian local ring', and subword pieces of terms like 'racemates', 'transistors', 'voltammetry'. The concepts involved are mixed.

Fires on 'of' right after a purpose noun at the start of a statement of aims: 'The purpose of', 'The aim of', 'The goal of', 'The main purpose of' (typical of abstracts: 'The purpose of this study was to'). Other noun+preposition frames ('wrong with', 'Here's') fire weakly to moderately.

Fires on non-initial subword pieces inside rare, foreign or proper-noun words split into several tokens (e.g. 'h[uk]uk', 'St[ur]ridge', 'R[AV]4', 'ch[ym]otrypsin', 'nucleus [acc]umbens'), including non-English text and CJK. Common whole words fire weakly.

Mostly fires on subword pieces of rare names and technical terms (scopolamine, microcalorimetry, immunosorbent, Svartholm, Hilbert, proliferator), but there is also a scattering of unrelated tokens ('of' in 'law of excluded middle', 'World', list punctuation in code). A loose mixture.

Fires strongly on CJK characters inside running Chinese/Japanese text. It also fires moderately on recurring tokens in licence boilerplate ('to use', 'it and/or modify', ' *' comment lines) and on sentence-final periods in expository prose. These look like several unrelated jobs.

Unclear mixture: subword pieces of non-English words (Finnish, German, Vietnamese, Indonesian), shell flag dashes ('grep -i', '-mtime'), the hyphen in 'p,p'-DDE', 'PRE' in 'PRECEDENTIAL', and assorted code tokens. No common thread is evident.
